26 A stationary wave is formed on a stretched string. The diagram illustrates the string at an instant
of time when the displacement of the string is at its maximum.
string
fixed
point
fixed
point
P
The frequency of the wave is 250 Hz. Point P on the string has a vertical displacement of –1.0 mm.
What will be the vertical displacement of the point P after a time of 5 ms?
A
–1.0 mm
B
zero
C
+0.5 mm
D
+1.0 mm

hints: Notice point P is at the trough of the stationary wave, so it is an antinode at its maximum negative displacement of $-1.0 \text{ mm}$ at $t = 0$.
Use $T = 1/f$ with $f = 250 \text{ Hz}$ to find the oscillation period of P, then express the given $5 \text{ ms}$ as a number of periods.
Recall each point on a stationary wave performs SHM: from an extreme it returns after one period and passes through zero after a quarter period.
walkthrough: Find the period of oscillation of any point on the string from $T = 1/f$. With $f = 250 \text{ Hz}$, $T = 1/250 = 0.004 \text{ s} = 4.0 \text{ ms}$.
Express the elapsed time as a fraction of a period: $5 \text{ ms} / 4.0 \text{ ms} = 1.25$, so the motion is one full oscillation plus one quarter of an oscillation.
Point P is at an antinode and starts at maximum displacement $-1.0 \text{ mm}$. In SHM, after one full period it returns to $-1.0 \text{ mm}$.
A further quarter period takes it from the extreme to the equilibrium position, where displacement is zero.
Zero displacement after $1.25T$ is option B.

A.explanation: This would be the displacement after a whole number of periods, but $5 \text{ ms}$ is not a whole number of periods for $250 \text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: After $1.25$ periods the antinode moves from maximum negative displacement through a full oscillation plus a quarter oscillation to the equilibrium position, so displacement is zero.

C.explanation: Point P oscillates between $-1.0 \text{ mm}$ and $+1.0 \text{ mm}$ with SHM, and $+0.5 \text{ mm}$ does not correspond to $1.25$ periods from an extreme.

D.explanation: This is the opposite extreme, reached after a half period of $2.0 \text{ ms}$, not after $5 \text{ ms}$.
